body.translated_text: <s>Kṣemendra</s>: <s>Kalāvilāsa</s> (Display of Arts)

children.translated_text: resplendent and radiant with gems, like the chest of <s>Śrīpati</s> (Viṣṇu). // 1.1 //

body.translated_text: There is a vast city, auspicious as the abode of the embrace of <s>Kamalā</s> (Lakṣmī),

children.translated_text: always bears the mansions, as if dividing himself into many forms. // 1.2 //

body.translated_text: Where <s>Śeṣa</s>, the serpent, with the multitude of hanging pearls reflected in the jeweled ground,

children.translated_text: shines as an obstacle for <s>abhisārikā</s> (women going to meet their lovers), like a robber tearing away the curtain of night's darkness. // 1.3 //

body.translated_text: Where the mass of buildings, dazzling with the radiance of crystal,

children.translated_text: lives on, sustained by the nectar of the radiance of the moon-faced women's faces. // 1.4 //

body.translated_text: Where the mind-born one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), behaving like a moth to the flames of the fire of <s>Trinayana</s>'s (Śiva's) eye,

children.translated_text: have their bodies perfumed by the fragrance of flowers fallen from loosened hair. // 1.5 //

body.translated_text: Where the breezes, carrying streams of water drops from the exertion of beautiful women wearied by love-play,

children.translated_text: spreads like the tinkling of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s anklets. // 1.6 //

body.translated_text: Where in the lotus groves, the sweet sound of young swans, their voices hoarse from swallowing tender lotus stalks,

children.translated_text: always appears like the embodiment of the rainy season, with its masses of rain-bearing clouds and rainbows. // 1.7 //

body.translated_text: Where the row of emerald fountain-houses with dancing, charming peacocks,

children.translated_text: shine like <s>Apsarases</s> standing upon the milky waves of the nectar-ocean. // 1.8 //

body.translated_text: Where in the crystal palaces veiled in moonbeams, the doe-eyed women

children.translated_text: the foremost among all repositories of arts, named <s>Śrī Mūladeva</s>. // 1.9 //

body.translated_text: There lived one who surpassed hundreds of hosts of great illusionists in deceit,

children.translated_text: attained vast prosperity through his own virtues, like a universal sovereign. // 1.10 //

body.translated_text: He, of exceeding wealth, being relied upon by tricksters who came from various countries and regions,

children.translated_text: a merchant approached him, having presented gifts of precious gems and gold. // 1.11 //

body.translated_text: Once, after the meal, as he was seated in the assembly hall with connoisseurs,

children.translated_text: having been offered a seat with honor, spoke after resting a moment: // 1.12 //

body.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyagupta</s>, bowing, accompanied by his son <s>Candragupta</s>,

children.translated_text: like a village woman in the city, does not quite attain confidence. // 1.13 //

body.translated_text: "This speech of one such as me before you, with its boldness born of long familiarity,

children.translated_text: like the innate radiance of the sun, makes the directions free from darkness. // 1.14 //

body.translated_text: Your splendid mass of rays of wisdom, which eclipses <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s intellect,

children.text: eko mamaiṣa sūnuḥ saṃjātaḥ paścime vayasi // 1.15 //
children.translated_text: this one son was born in my old age. // 1.15 //

body.translated_text: Of me, whose treasury is filled with manifold gems, pearls, and gold accumulated from birth,

children.translated_text: and accumulations of wealth are as fickle as water drops on a lotus leaf swaying in the wind. // 1.16 //

body.translated_text: Youth is the abode of delusion, and adolescence too brings the madness of passion;

children.translated_text: this chain of vices has befallen this son of mine. // 1.17 //

body.translated_text: Captivating doe-eyed women, tricksters who are bees to the lotus of pleasures—

children.translated_text: who become balls in the hands of tricksters, and jewels in the anklets of courtesans. // 1.18 //

body.translated_text: There is no liberation for the naive ones who are born in wealthy households,

children.translated_text: the naive are devoured by trickster-cats like young birds. // 1.19 //

body.translated_text: Ignorant of place and time, fickle-faced, though lame yet leaping,

children.text: na yathā prayāti nāśaṃ tathāsya buddhiṃ prayaccha parām // 1.20 //
children.translated_text: please bestow upon him the highest wisdom so that he does not go to ruin." // 1.20 //

body.translated_text: This son of a dependent is truly dearer than your own son, O learned one;

children.translated_text: <s>Mūladeva</s> spoke to him, with the tips of his lips spread in a wave of delight: // 1.21 //

body.translated_text: Having understood the fitting words spoken by him whose head was bowed in humility,

body.text: āstāmeṣa sutaste mama bhavane nija iva prayatnaparaḥ &

children.translated_text: he shall gradually learn the entire heart of the arts, as taught by me. // 1.22 //"

body.translated_text: "Let this son of yours stay in my house as if he were my own, devoted to effort;

body.text: iti tasya śāsanena svasutaṃ niḥkṣaipya tadgṛhe matimān &

children.translated_text: bowing, departed to his own residence, delighted. // 1.23 //

body.translated_text: Thus, by his instruction, the wise merchant, having placed his son in that house,

children.translated_text: gradually became invisible, like a gambler defeated by tricksters. // 1.24 //

body.translated_text: Then the sun, with loosened web of rays, smoky in hue, stripped of its garments,

children.translated_text: shone forth like the pink-red hue of sindūra powder. // 1.25 //

body.translated_text: When the day-maker set, the twilight, joined with the elephant of the mass of darkness,

children.text: na tu raktāpi hi sandhyā hṛdayaṃ jānāti kaḥ strīṇām // 1.26 //
children.translated_text: but the twilight, though passionate, did not—who indeed knows the heart of women? // 1.26 //

body.translated_text: Though abandoned every day, the daylight followed the sun;

children.translated_text: the darkness wandered about in confusion, unsteady, like the flitting of a bee. // 1.27 //

body.translated_text: When the reddening twilight departed gradually somewhere from the lotus garden of the sky's courtyard,

children.text: tīvro'pi janasya sadāyātaḥ khalu vallabho bhavati // 1.28 //
children.translated_text: indeed, however harsh, one who is always present becomes dear to people. // 1.28 //

body.translated_text: The earth became as if closed shut by the darkness, like swoons of separation from the sun;

children.translated_text: like a <s>Śabara</s> (tribal) woman adorned with ornaments of peacock feathers gathered from the familiar darkness. // 1.29 //

body.translated_text: The night shone beautifully, adorned with garlands of white and brighter stars like pearl necklaces,

children.translated_text: the messenger that awakens the night-lilies, and the cause of distress for <s>cakravākī</s> birds. // 1.30 //

body.translated_text: Then gradually arose the moonlight, which burns the wives of travelers,

children.translated_text: shone resplendently, the white tilaka-mark of the beloved of the night. // 1.31 //

body.translated_text: The pure lord of the night, the white parasol of <s>Manmatha</s> (Kāma), the crystal mirror of the ladies of the directions,

children.translated_text: gleamed on the bank of the celestial river like a royal swan. // 1.32 //

body.translated_text: The moon, of white radiance, sporting like a bracelet on the lotus-stalk vine of its own rays,

children.translated_text: and through that, there was the play of the doe-eyed women, their hearts delighted with passion. // 1.33 //

body.translated_text: The dark night was beautiful with the moon, and with it <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) held his spring festival,

children.translated_text: joyfully entered the blossoming clusters of night-lilies, like bees their abodes. // 1.34 //

body.translated_text: The tricksters, ministers of prosperity, abandoning the lotus that had lost its luster,

children.translated_text: wearing garlands of bones made from rows of stars, the night shone like a <s>Kāpālikī</s> (female ascetic). // 1.35 //

body.translated_text: Smeared with the ashes of moonlight, with beautiful skull-like crescents of the moon,

children.translated_text: in his own jeweled garden-palace, having completed his meditation and contemplation, // 1.36 //

body.translated_text: At that time, when everything was illuminated by the spreading rays of the full moon,

children.translated_text: surrounded at his footstool by his chief disciples, <s>Kandalī</s> and others, // 1.37 //

body.translated_text: seated on a crystal seat, with the moon as his inseparable friend,

children.translated_text: making the moonlight seem shy and withdrawn with the radiance of his teeth: // 1.38 //

body.translated_text: <s>Mūladeva</s> spoke, gazing long at the merchant's son before him,

children.translated_text: knowing which, even the fickle and momentary fortunes become stable. // 1.39 //

body.translated_text: "Listen, son, to the extremely cunning essence of the heart of all arts of deceivers,

children.translated_text: into which naive deer fall, with no support. // 1.40 //

body.translated_text: In this forest of worldly existence, there is one well, concealed by a net of grass and leaves—

children.translated_text: its mouth is covered by crooked serpents of deception, and it stands thus in the world. // 1.41 //

body.translated_text: That treasure-pot, named <s>dambha</s> (hypocrisy), is by nature profound;

children.translated_text: the source of power for tricksters, the means of bringing <s>Śrī</s> (fortune) under control. // 1.42 //

body.translated_text: <s>Dambha</s> is the secret mantra of illusion, the wish-fulfilling gem for desired objects,

body.text: matsyāsyevāpsu sadā dambhasya jñāyate gatiḥ kena &

children.text: nāsya karau na ca pādau na śiro durlakṣya evāsau // 1.43 //
children.translated_text: It has no hands, no feet, no head—it is truly imperceptible. // 1.43 //

body.translated_text: Like the movement of a fish in water, who can ever perceive the course of hypocrisy?

children.translated_text: birds by nets spread on land, and human beings by hypocrisy. // 1.44 //

body.translated_text: Serpents are caught by the power of mantras, naive deer by cunning traps,

children.translated_text: ever victorious, imperceptible, <s>dambha</s> (hypocrisy) rises like a cloud of illusion! // 1.45 //

body.translated_text: The deception of people's hearts, the pillar of illusion, the commencement of world-conquest—

children.translated_text: <s>dambha</s> (hypocrisy) is the root and the hub. // 1.46 //

body.translated_text: In this vast wheel of circular deception, whirling with constant vortexes, with a thousand unbearable crooked spokes,

children.translated_text: the tree of hypocrisy bears flowers of purity and fruits on hundreds of branches of happiness. // 1.47 //

body.translated_text: Rooted in closing the eyes, long watered by drops from the wet topknot after bathing,

children.translated_text: and the terrible cat-hypocrisy through stealthy gait and restrained eyes. // 1.48 //

body.translated_text: There is the crane-hypocrisy through vows and observances, and the tortoise-hypocrisy through concealed restraints,

children.translated_text: but cat-hypocrisy alone has attained universal sovereignty among all hypocrisies. // 1.49 //

body.translated_text: Crane-hypocrisy is the lord of hypocrisies, and tortoise-hypocrisy the king of hypocrisies,

children.translated_text: a ghost of excessive mud-smearing, speaking sparingly, with carefully placed footwear, // 1.50 //

body.translated_text: With closely trimmed nails, beard, and hair, either with a topknot or matted locks, or with a long tuft,

children.translated_text: his arms constrained by the tips of a bark garment tucked under his arm, as if carrying a vessel, // 1.51 //

body.translated_text: with a thick-knotted sacred thread marking his ears, and a golden string placed on his back,

children.translated_text: with lips trembling from prayer, absorbed in meditation on the public streets, // 1.52 //

body.translated_text: displaying learning through various disputes involving finger-counting and computation,

children.translated_text: obstructing all people, again and again touching the corners of his ears, // 1.53 //

body.translated_text: with elaborately performed sipping rituals and long immersions at a sacred ford,

children.translated_text: with broad tilaka marks indicating complete ceremonial worship of the gods, // 1.54 //

body.translated_text: with hissing teeth sounds advertising the unbearable cold of winter bathing,

body.text: śirasā bibarti kusumaṃ vinipatitāṃ kākadṛṣṭim iva racayan &

children.text: evaṃ rūpaṃ puruṣo yo yaḥ sa sa dāmbhiko jñeyaḥ // 1.55 //
children.translated_text: whoever is of such a form—he should be known as a hypocrite. // 1.55 //

body.translated_text: bearing a flower on his head while casting a crow-like sideways glance,

children.translated_text: a friend of compassion to the townsfolk, seeking fame—such is the hypocritical trickster. // 1.56 //

body.translated_text: Bowed before by the unworthy, stiff before the worthy, hateful toward his own kin,

children.translated_text: with furrowed brows and silent once his purpose is accomplished—the hypocrite is cruel. // 1.57 //

body.translated_text: At the time of needing a favor, bowing his head and uttering hundreds of flatteries,

children.translated_text: that very <s>dambha</s> (hypocrisy) now dwells on the earth's surface in the bodies of beings. // 1.58 //

body.translated_text: The demon <s>Jambha</s>, who formerly obstructed the prosperity of the gods—

children.text: niḥspṛhadambhasya tulāṃ yānti tu naite śatāṃśena // 1.59 //
children.translated_text: these do not equal even a hundredth part of the hypocrisy of the renunciant. // 1.59 //

body.translated_text: The hypocrisy of purity, the hypocrisy of tranquility, the hypocrisy of the graduate, and the hypocrisy of meditation—

children.translated_text: through the hypocrisy of purity, this person attains the status of a <s>Viśvāmitra</s>. // 1.60 //

body.translated_text: Quarreling about cleanliness and conduct, wearing away earth, touching his own kinsmen—

children.translated_text: the constant hypocrisy of non-violence is a submarine fire that devours everything. // 1.61 //

body.translated_text: Having gathered many kinds of living beings, exceedingly thirsty for the waters of deposited wealth,

body.text: muṇḍo jaṭilo nagnaśchatrī daṇḍī kaṣāyacārī vā &

children.text: bhasmasmeraśarīro diśi diśi bhogī vijṛmbhate dambhaḥ // 1.62 //
children.translated_text: with body smeared in ashes, hypocrisy expands its enjoyments in every direction. // 1.62 //

body.translated_text: Whether shaven, matted-haired, naked, umbrella-bearing, staff-bearing, or wearing ochre robes,

children.translated_text: whether with head wrapped in cloth or wearing a turban peaked like a shrine, // 1.63 //

body.translated_text: Whether bald, stout-bodied, emaciated, or in the guise of a sage,

body.text: lobhaḥ pitātivṛddho jananī māyā sahodaraḥ kūṭaḥ &

children.translated_text: crookedness of form his wife, and the arrogant roar is the son of hypocrisy. // 1.64 //

body.translated_text: Greed is his aged father, <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) his mother, fraud his brother,

body.text: bhagavānpurā svayaṃbhūḥ kṛtvā bhuvanāni bhūtasargaṃ ca &

children.translated_text: stood long absorbed in thought, his activity having ceased. // 1.65 //

body.translated_text: The blessed <s>Svayambhū</s> (Brahmā), having created the worlds and the beings,

children.translated_text: unable to obtain the enjoyment of wealth and such things through the special practice of uprightness, // 1.66 //

body.translated_text: Seeing with his divine sight the mortals in the human world without support,

children.translated_text: he created <s>dambha</s> (hypocrisy) for the prosperity of men, as the basis of esteem. // 1.67 //

body.translated_text: with eyes closed, having quickly entered the state of <s>samādhi</s> consisting of illusion,

children.translated_text: a staff with a curved horn like his own crooked heart, a black antelope skin, and a spade, // 1.68 //

body.translated_text: Bearing a bundle of <s>kuśa</s> grass, a string of manuscripts, an empty water-pot,

children.translated_text: with clearly shaven head and a white flower at the base of his topknot wrapped in <s>kuśa</s> grass, // 1.69 //

body.translated_text: with ears marked by a thick <s>kuśa</s>-grass ring of purification, with the purification ring on his hand,

children.translated_text: with a bracelet of <s>rudrākṣa</s> beads on his hand, carrying a vessel filled with earth, // 1.70 //

body.translated_text: with neck stiff as wood, lips trembling with prayer, eyes absorbed in meditation,

children.translated_text: a silent one who communicates all his heart's desires through manifold signs of disdain, // 1.71 //

body.translated_text: with angry sidelong glances, knitted brows, a face expressing commands through murmurs,

children.translated_text: <s>Dambha</s> (Hypocrisy) stood before him, having risen, desiring a seat. // 1.72 //

body.translated_text: guarding against others' touch, seeking purity even in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,

body.text: ākalpena sumahatā sahasāsya vaśīkṛtāḥ paraṃ tena &

children.translated_text: even the Seven Sages bowed before him and stood with folded hands. // 1.73 //

body.translated_text: By that grand appearance, he immediately brought under his sway;

children.translated_text: stood motionless yet trembling with awe, wonder, and delight. // 1.74 //

body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (Brahmā), though he had playfully created the entire host of creation,

children.translated_text: and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s back was bent with shame at his own inferior vows and austerities. // 1.75 //

body.translated_text: Due to his exceedingly severe austerities, <s>Agastya</s> was as if swallowed up in great astonishment,

children.translated_text: and <s>Nārada</s> was rendered disrespected, lacking the pomp in his own austerities. // 1.76 //

body.translated_text: And <s>Kautsa</s> squinted, being reproached for his own overly simple sage's vows,

children.translated_text: and <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was frightened, and <s>Gālava</s> with curled neck, and <s>Bhṛgu</s> was submerged. // 1.77 //

body.translated_text: And <s>Jamadagni</s>, with face sunken to the level of his own knee-joints,

children.translated_text: motionless before them, with body heavy and stiff from no small pride, as if impaled on a trident, // 1.78 //

body.translated_text: With gaze fixed upon the lotus-seat, from which he had risen long ago in extreme anger,

children.translated_text: his ten faces blooming with radiance, as if laughing at his vehicle, the swan: // 1.79 //

body.translated_text: knowing that he desired a seat, the four-faced god (<s>Brahmā</s>) spoke with delight,

children.translated_text: you are worthy of this, which accords with the dignity arising from your host of virtues. // 1.80 //"

body.translated_text: "Sit, O son, upon my lap; by your observances, most extraordinary and supreme,

children.translated_text: having sprinkled a handful of water, with difficulty sat down—that <s>Dambha</s> (Hypocrisy). // 1.81 //

body.translated_text: Thus addressed by the Creator of the universe, he, with hesitation yet without fear, upon that lap,

body.text: dambha uvāca // noccairvācyamavaśyaṃ yadi vācyaṃ hastapadmena &

children.text: ācchādya vaktrarandhraṃ spṛṣṭo na syāṃ yathāsyavātāṃśaiḥ // 1.82 //
children.translated_text: covering the opening of the mouth, so that I may not be touched by the gusts of breath." (1.82)

body.translated_text: <s>Dambha</s> (Hypocrisy) said: "One should not speak loudly; if something must be said, with a lotus-hand

children.translated_text: and said, "You are <s>Dambha</s> (Hypocrisy)!" gently shaking his fingertip. (1.83)

body.translated_text: Then, seeing his incomparable purity, <s>Brahmā</s> smiled

children.text: avatīrya bhuṅkṣvā bhogānvibudhairapi tattvato na vijñātaḥ // 1.84 //
children.translated_text: and enjoy pleasures not truly understood even by the gods." (1.84)

body.translated_text: "Arise! Descend upon the entire earth, girdled by the ocean's moat-like waters,

children.translated_text: tying a disposition-cord around the necks of mortals, he descended to earth. (1.85)

body.translated_text: Thus respectfully dismissed by <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), for those beings lost in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

body.text: atha martyalokametya bhrāntvā dambho vanāni nagarāṇi &

children.translated_text: and planting his victory-banner in the <s>Gauḍa</s> region, went forth in all directions. (1.86)

body.translated_text: Then, having come to the mortal world, <s>Dambha</s> wandered through forests and cities,

children.translated_text: in the authority of warriors—<s>Dambha</s> is everywhere, but especially among the <s>Gauḍas</s>. (1.87)

body.translated_text: In the speech of the <s>Bāhlīkas</s>, in the vows and observances of the easterners and southerners,

children.text: kurvanti ye prabhāte yatastato bhasmanā tilakam // 1.88 //
children.translated_text: make a forehead-mark with ashes from anywhere each morning— (1.88)

body.translated_text: Those who, aided by <s>Dambha</s>, with powder obtained from gifts and <s>śrāddha</s> ceremonies,

children.translated_text: <s>Dambha</s> perpetually dwells embodied in the mouths of court officials. (1.89)

body.translated_text: swiftly dividing beings on the surface of the earth into a thousand portions,

children.translated_text: the crooked hearts of appointees—this initiation of hearts is <s>Dambha</s> himself. (1.90)

body.translated_text: First he entered the heart of teachers, then the hearts of children and ascetics,

children.translated_text: and of actors, soldiers, singers, reciters, and wandering spies. (1.91)

body.translated_text: Then the hearts of astrologers, physicians, servants, merchants along with goldsmiths,

children.translated_text: <s>Dambha</s> afterwards entered even the interior of trees here. (1.92)

body.translated_text: Having entered the hearts of all creatures through portions of various transformations,

body.text: matsyārthī carati tapaḥ suciraṃ niḥspanda ekapādena &

children.translated_text: at the sacred fords—that crane-ascetic is the reason <s>Dambha</s> has entered the birds. (1.93)

body.translated_text: Desiring fish, the crane performs austerities for a long time, motionless on one leg

children.translated_text: that the trees desire water—this too is a manifestation of <s>Dambha</s>. (1.94)

body.translated_text: Bearing great matted locks and bark garments, constantly emaciated by cold, heat, and wind,

children.translated_text: when he is recognized in his various forms, the deceit of deceivers becomes fruitless. (1.95)

body.translated_text: Thus should <s>Dambha</s>, who is everywhere and always in every heart, be examined;

children.translated_text: formerly, by the <s>Vāmana</s>-trick, <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) conquered the three worlds. (1.96)

body.translated_text: This transformation of <s>Dambha</s> is a wish-fulfilling tree before the circle of cheats;
Canto 2

body.text: lobhaḥ sadā vicintyo lubdhebhyaḥ sarvato bhayaṃ dṛṣṭam &

children.translated_text: For one seized by greed, there is no discrimination between what should and should not be done. (2.1)

body.translated_text: <s>Lobha</s> (Greed) should always be considered; from the greedy, danger is seen everywhere.

children.translated_text: <s>Lobha</s> is the root cause, the demon of hoarded wealth, the all-devouring one. (2.2)

body.translated_text: Of deception, fraud, confusion, denial, trickery, cunning, and cheating—

children.translated_text: <s>Lobha</s> entered a pit—the crooked heart of shopkeepers. (2.3)

body.translated_text: Conquered by those possessing goodness, tranquility, austerity, true wealth, and scriptural knowledge,

children.text: ete hi divasacaurā muṣṇanti mudā janaṃ vaṇijaḥ // 2.4 //
children.translated_text: these merchants, who are daytime thieves, rob people with delight. (2.4)

body.translated_text: By fraudulent buying and selling, false weights, light measures, deceitful depositing and guarding—

children.translated_text: the shopkeeper distributes at home, with great difficulty, merely three cowrie shells. (2.5)

body.translated_text: Having stolen people's wealth all day through various fraudulent tricks,

children.translated_text: yet, as if bitten by black serpents, he recoils from charity and righteousness. (2.6)

body.translated_text: Fond of stories, he always goes to hear sacred books,

children.text: suciraṃ snānaṃ kurute na dadāti kapardikāmekām // 2.7 //
children.translated_text: he bathes for a long time but does not give even a single cowrie. (2.7)

body.translated_text: On the twelfth day, on the day of the ancestors, at the solstice, during eclipses of the sun and moon,

body.text: dattvā diśi diśi dṛṣṭiṃ yācakacakito'vaguṇṭhanaṃ kṛtvā &

children.translated_text: like a thief moving crookedly, he flees through winding alleys. (2.8)

body.translated_text: Casting his gaze in every direction, terrified of beggars, veiling himself,

body.text: na dadāti prativacanaṃ vikrayakāle śaṭho vaṇiṅmaunī &

children.translated_text: but seeing a man with deposit-money in hand, he begins a conversation. (2.9)

body.translated_text: The deceitful merchant, a silent one at the time of sale, gives no reply,

body.text: uttiṣṭhati namati vaṇik pṛcchati kuśalaṃ dadāti ca sthānaṃ &

children.translated_text: seeing a man with deposit-money in hand, and initiates a righteous conversation. (2.10)

body.translated_text: The merchant stands up, bows, inquires about well-being, and offers a seat,

body.text: kaścidvadati tametya draviṇaṃ niḥkṣipya hanta gantāsmi &

children.text: bhrātaḥ paraṃ prabhāte viṣṭidinaṃ kiṃ karomyadya // 2.11 //
children.translated_text: brother, but tomorrow is a compulsory labor day—what shall I do today?' (2.11)

body.translated_text: Someone comes to him and says, 'Having deposited this money, alas, I must go;

body.text: paśuriva vaktuṃ kartuṃ kiṃcidayaṃ mama patirna jānāti &

children.translated_text: having said thus to her own people at home, the woman conducts a man's affairs. // 3.18 //

body.translated_text: "My husband, like an animal, does not know how to say or do anything"—

children.translated_text: and speaks loudly in the house—such is the wife of one who is as good as dead. // 3.19 //

body.translated_text: She rises to greet visitors, herself goes and comes on errands of business,

children.translated_text: an artisan's wife, a forest woman, a miser's wife, or a merchant's wife— // 3.20 //

body.translated_text: A jealous elderly wife, a servant's wife, or a government official's wife,

children.translated_text: engaged in counting others' virtues, constantly speaking of her own husband's faults, // 3.21 //

body.translated_text: fond of attending gatherings, naturally affectionate toward young people,

children.translated_text: a naive bride, proud of her mastery of all arts, distressed by the company of the lowly, // 3.22 //

body.translated_text: of little wealth but many pleasures, either beautiful or the wife of an ugly husband,

children.translated_text: with many unchaste friends, naturally partial to heroic men, // 3.23 //

body.translated_text: addicted to gambling and drinking, skilled in lengthy stories, singing, and passion,

children.translated_text: quick with retorts, devoid of truthfulness, shameless by nature, // 3.24 //

body.translated_text: having abandoned household duties, assuming various disguises, practicing unrestricted conduct,

children.translated_text: in private reveling in the pomp of various amusements, in public reciting the <s>Sāvitrī</s> prayer, // 3.25 //

body.translated_text: devoted to inquiring about the welfare of others, with speech pleasant and affectionate,

children.translated_text: independently arranging feasts, drinks, extravagant outings, and festivals, // 3.26 //

body.translated_text: devoted to visiting sacrifices, sacred fords, temples, astrologers, physicians, and relatives' houses,

children.translated_text: eager for darśana (audiences) and initiations, detached from her beloved, absorbed in <s>samādhi</s> (meditation), // 3.27 //

body.translated_text: devoted to mendicants and ascetics, indifferent to her own people, attached to charming things,
with assembly-entertaining friends—she should be known as one of ruined character. (a cluster verse) // 3.28 //

children.translated_text: women are twilights, she-demons, stealers of the color of passion, cruel. // 3.29 //

body.translated_text: With the constant fault of attachment, deluding people, seizing like many planets, fickle,

children.translated_text: who, pleased and inclined to tranquility, are unrestrained with fickle women. // 3.30 //

body.translated_text: Who is not worthy of bearing the yoke? Those of naive minds, attached to trivial pursuits,

children.translated_text: this alone is the means of bringing them under control, without mantras or magical devices. // 3.31 //

body.translated_text: Boasting of romantic exploits and valor, various descriptions of extravagant gifts—

children.text: strīṇāṃ nṛśamsacaritaiḥ kasya na saṃjāyate kampaḥ // 3.32 //
children.translated_text: whose heart does not tremble at their cruel deeds? // 3.32 //

body.translated_text: Of women, who are night-wanderers in the dark night of the <s>Kali</s> age, with their thousand <s>māyās</s> (illusions),

children.translated_text: named <s>Dhanadatta</s>, a repository of gems like the ocean. // 3.33 //

body.translated_text: There was on earth a renowned lord of merchants, whose splendor surpassed that of <s>Dhanapati</s> (<s>Kubera</s>),

children.translated_text: named <s>Vasumatī</s>, who conquered the directions with the play of her eyes. // 3.34 //

body.translated_text: His prosperity manifested as his daughter, of graceful limbs, as if the embodiment of <s>Manobhava</s> (Kāma),

body.text: pradadau sa tāmaputraḥ putrapade vinihitāṃ priyāṃ putrīṃ &

children.translated_text: to a merchant named <s>Samudradatta</s>, equal in wealth and noble lineage. // 3.35 //

body.translated_text: He, being without a son, gave his dear daughter, placed in the position of a son,

body.text: ramamāṇaḥ sa tayā saha hariṇākṣyā śvasuramandire suciram &

children.translated_text: he once departed ahead of a caravan returning from the islands. // 3.36 //

body.translated_text: Delighting with her, the doe-eyed one, in his father-in-law's mansion for a long time,

children.translated_text: sported there, the very ground of grace, playfully restless with her friends. // 3.37 //

body.translated_text: When her husband had gone, the young woman, having ascended to the top of the palace in her father's house,

body.text: saudhe manmatharūpaṃ pṛthunayanā pathi dadarśa puruṣaṃ sā &

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣtvaiva gatāsyāḥ kvāpi dhṛtiḥ kumatikupiteva // 3.38 //
children.translated_text: upon seeing whom her composure fled somewhere, as if angered by her wicked thoughts. // 3.38 //

body.translated_text: On the terrace, the large-eyed woman saw on the street a man of the form of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love),

body.text: sā tena capalanayanā sahasā muṣiteva hāritavicārā &

children.translated_text: became utterly unable to conceal the transformation wrought by desire. // 3.39 //

body.translated_text: She, with restless eyes, as if suddenly robbed by him, her judgment gone,

body.text: śīlaṃ pālasya capale mā pātaya nimnageva kulakūlam &

children.translated_text: thus her girdle, jingling with trembling and agitation, seemed to admonish her loudly for a long time. // 3.40 //

body.translated_text: "Protect your virtue, O fickle one! Do not cause the bank of your family to collapse like a river!"—

body.text: sā kṛtvāḷviditakathāṃ rahasi sakhīmānināya taṃ taruṇam &

children.text: calitaṃ hi kāminīnāṃ dhartuṃ śaknoti kaścittam // 3.41 //
children.translated_text: for who can restrain the wavering heart of amorous women? // 3.41 //

body.translated_text: She, having made a confidante aware of the matter, secretly brought that young man;

children.translated_text: with the dwelling-place of natural love, that wanton woman rejoiced with him. // 3.42 //

body.translated_text: With the blossoming of desire, with the graces of lovemaking, with delightful jests and humor,

children.translated_text: entered his father-in-law's residence with great pomp. // 3.43 //

body.translated_text: Then <s>Samudradatta</s>, having completed his business affairs, hastening, anxious to see his beloved,

children.text: ativāhya dinaṃ dayitāsahitaḥ śayyāgṛhaṃ sa yayau // 3.44 //
children.translated_text: he went to the bedchamber together with his beloved. // 3.44 //

body.translated_text: Having passed the day amidst people busy with grand festive celebrations and heaps of luxurious goods,

children.translated_text: with fragrant incense wafting, like a celestial abode, with gleaming jeweled lamps, // 3.45 //

body.translated_text: On a bed prepared most excellently, in a canopied, delightful chamber,

children.text: madagaja iva navanalinīṃ bheje ratilālasaḥ śayyām // 3.46 //
children.translated_text: like a rutting elephant approaching a fresh lotus pond, sought the bed, eager for love. // 3.46 //

body.translated_text: there he, embracing his beloved whose lotus-eyes were rolling with the intoxication of wine,

children.translated_text: stood with closed eyes, absorbed in contemplation like a <s>yoginī</s>, for a long time. // 3.47 //

body.translated_text: But she, her attention fixed on the meditation of another man dwelling within her heart,

children.translated_text: with limbs contracted before her husband, she remembered only that stealer of her virtue. // 3.48 //

body.translated_text: During embraces, kisses, and the loosening of garments, sighing excessively,

children.translated_text: prostrated himself and with flatteries begged for something to appease her. // 3.49 //

body.translated_text: Thinking she was sulking out of love, the naive husband <s>Samudradatta</s>

children.translated_text: to women who are passionate for another man, who turn away, and who display coyness feigning love-quarrels. // 3.50 //

body.translated_text: Foolish men, beasts among men, are attracted all the more

children.translated_text: the sun is passionate even toward the twilight, though she is dyed by a hundred other hues. // 3.51 //

body.translated_text: What can be done? This desire goes to another, and desire is self-willed;

children.text: saṃcintya ciraṃ svapatiṃ viṣamiva saṃmūrchitā mene // 3.52 //
children.translated_text: regarded her own husband as if he were poison, and swooned. // 3.52 //

body.translated_text: She, thinking long of her lover placed at an appointed meeting in a hidden garden bower,

children.translated_text: she rose, adorned herself, and stood quietly, ready to depart. // 3.53 //

body.translated_text: When <s>Samudradatta</s>, his eyes sealed with sleep, was wearied by her feigned affection,

body.text: cauraḥ kṣaṇe ca tasminmugdhamattajanaṃ praviśya tadbhavanam &

children.translated_text: and saw her, unnoticed, eager to go, her ornaments jingling. // 3.54 //

body.translated_text: At that very moment, a thief entered the house of the deluded, sleeping people,

children.translated_text: slowly drew close, closing its eyes even tighter. // 3.55 //

body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the moon, trembling as if startled, quickly embracing the horizon, beloved of the king of gods,

children.translated_text: like the deceitful smile of night. // 3.56 //

body.translated_text: The moon spread its cool rays upon the night, whose lotuses had contracted and whose night-lilies bloomed gloriously,

children.translated_text: the ponds, heavy with the humming of swarms of bees among the clusters of night-lilies, seemed to laugh. // 3.57 //

body.translated_text: Seeing the sky, weary from the sun's heat, now joyful with the spreading moon,

children.translated_text: as if bashful, with a veil of bees drawn by the fragrance of night-lotuses before her. (3.58)

body.translated_text: The night-goddess seized the sky, her covering garment of darkness removed by the moon's rays,

body.text: suptajane'tha niśārdhe candrāloke ca vipulatāṃ yāte &

children.translated_text: fearless as if in darkness, she slowly made her way to the garden. (3.59)

body.translated_text: Then, at midnight, when people were asleep and the moonlight had grown vast,

body.text: atha sā viveśa vivaśā viṣamaśaraploṣitā nijopavanam &

children.translated_text: secretly followed by an astonished thief attracted by her ornaments. (3.60)

body.translated_text: Then she, helpless, scorched by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love), entered her own garden,

children.translated_text: arousing suspicion in the grove, noticed by the birds— (3.61)

body.translated_text: There she saw her beloved, adorned, wearing brilliant and elegant garments, with gleaming flowers,

children.translated_text: burned by the hand-fires of the moon whose radiance played across the horizons— (3.62)

body.translated_text: scorched by the flames of separation from his heart's beloved,

children.translated_text: his life departed as he hung from a vine clinging to a tree branch. (3.63)

body.translated_text: having waited long at the meeting-place, despairing of reunion with his beloved,

children.translated_text: and the slender woman fell like a vine, with her jingling bracelets trembling. (3.64)

body.translated_text: Seeing him, she dissolved, wailing with grief, sorrow, and terror,

children.translated_text: slowly regaining her life, she lamented softly in a low voice: (3.65)

body.translated_text: With her eyes closed in a swoon, lying on the ground in an embrace for a long time,

body.text: hā hā nayanānanda kva nu te viśadendusundaraṃ vadanam &

children.text: drakṣyāmi mandapuṇyā kimidaṃ kvāhaṃ kva me kāntaḥ // 3.66 //
children.translated_text: Wretched am I! What is this? Where am I? Where is my beloved?' (3.66)

body.translated_text: 'Alas, alas, O delight of my eyes! Where now shall I see your face, beautiful as the bright moon?

body.text: iti taruṇakaruṇamabalā vilapya pāśaṃ vimucya yatnena &

children.text: aṅke dhṛtvāsya mukhaṃ cucumba jīvaṃ kṣipantīva // 3.67 //
children.translated_text: held his face in her lap and kissed it, as if casting life into him. (3.67)

body.translated_text: Thus the young helpless woman, lamenting piteously, with effort untying the noose,

body.text: sā tasya vadanakamalaṃ nijavadane mohitā kṛtvā &

children.translated_text: made the betel-offering, as if manifesting her embodied love. (3.68)

body.translated_text: She, deluded, placing the lotus of his face upon her own face,

children.translated_text: entering the corpse's body, cut off her nose. (3.69)

body.translated_text: Then a <s>vetāla</s> (vampire-spirit), summoned by the fragrance of her flower-heaps, musk-incense, and such,

children.translated_text: and entering her husband's house, shrieked loudly 'Alas!' (3.70)

body.translated_text: She, having obtained that fruit of misconduct brought about by desire's arrow, with her nose cut off, returned

children.text: sā nāsikā mameyaṃ bhartrā chinneti cakranda // 3.71 //
children.translated_text: she wailed, 'My nose has been cut off by my husband!' (3.71)

body.translated_text: When all the household was roused and <s>Samudradatta</s> was alarmed by the outcry,

children.text: vikrītaḥ paradeśe mūka ivoce na kiṃcidapi // 3.72 //
children.translated_text: was sold as it were to a foreign land, and like a mute, said not a single word. (3.72)

body.translated_text: When questioned by his angry relatives—father-in-law and others—<s>Samudradatta</s>

children.translated_text: the king's wrath fell upon <s>Samudradatta</s> with a heavy monetary punishment. (3.73)

body.translated_text: Then, at dawn, when his relatives reported the matter at the king's court,

children.translated_text: reported it before the king and received proper honor. (3.74)

body.translated_text: The thief too, having directly witnessed the entire affair, filled with amazement,

body.text: udyāne śavavadane tasyāstāṃ nāsikāṃ ca saṃdarśya &

children.translated_text: he brought about the vindication of <s>Samudradatta</s>, as befits a selfless friend. (3.75)

body.translated_text: By showing her nose at the corpse's face in the garden,

children.text: yo nāma vetti sa strībhirnaiva vañcyate matimān // 3.76 //
children.translated_text: he who truly knows them, that wise man, is never deceived by women. (3.76)

body.translated_text: Thus, these exceedingly crooked, cruel in conduct, shameless, and fickle women—
Canto 4

children.translated_text: by whose deceitful conduct even <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (<s>Kubera</s>) is reduced to an ascetic. (4.1)

body.translated_text: Among these, courtesans are even more crooked, stealing people's hearts with false love;

children.translated_text: like rivers into the ocean, the sixty-four arts reside in the hearts of courtesans. (4.2)

body.translated_text: Charming and most flirtatious, with many waves, flowing downward—

children.translated_text: the art of knowing desire, the art of seizing, and the art of deceiving friends. (4.3)

body.translated_text: The art of dress, the art of dance, the art of song, the art of sidelong glances,

children.translated_text: the art of kissing, the art of other things, and the art of shameless passionate frenzy. (4.4)

body.translated_text: The art of drinking, the art of play, the art of love-making, the art of pausing between embraces,

children.translated_text: the art of perspiration, confusion, and trembling, and the art of private grooming. (4.5)

body.translated_text: The art of quarrelsome jealousy-play, the art of weeping, the art of destroying pride,

children.translated_text: the art of unbearable passion in separation, and the art of firmly refusing reconciliation. (4.6)

body.translated_text: The art of closing the eyes, unbearable motionlessness, the art of appearing dead,

children.translated_text: the art of stealing, the art of caste-play, the art of dalliance, and the art of the thief and the king. (4.7)

body.translated_text: The art of quarreling with one's own mother, the art of joyfully gazing at a good household,

children.translated_text: the art of ailments, the art of massage, and the art of sleepy eyes and menstrual garments. (4.8)

body.translated_text: The art of relaxing dignity, the art of causeless fault-finding speech,

children.translated_text: and the art of praising the sight-tour of an abandoned lover. (4.9)

body.translated_text: The art of harshness, the art of severity, the art of placing hands on throat and door-bolt,

children.translated_text: the art of subjugation-medicines and spells, the art of tree-worship, and the art of hair-dyeing. (4.10)

body.translated_text: The art of carelessly strolling in sacred fords, gardens, and temples, and the domestic art,

children.translated_text: and the courtesan, exhausted by sixty-three arts, finally becomes a <s>kuṭṭanī</s> (procuress). (4.11)

body.translated_text: The art of various merits involving mendicants and ascetics, the art of showing island-shrines,

children.translated_text: yet fools with vain hopes seek even her genuine affection. (4.12)

body.translated_text: To those of unknown name and caste, she surrenders even herself for a share of wealth;

children.translated_text: is consumed by some broken, naked, wretched man devoid of all virtues. (4.13)

body.translated_text: The wealth earned by deceiving all people, impure, of those whose hearts are burned by passion—

children.translated_text: becomes the beloved of those who have cheated all people. (4.14)

body.translated_text: A low-born horse-rider, an elephant-keeper, or a most wicked craftsman

children.translated_text: the proud one went to <s>Vidarbha</s>, accompanied by his minister renowned for virtue and fame. (4.15)

body.translated_text: King <s>Vikramasiṃha</s>, defeated by powerful kings in the past,

body.text: tatra sa veśyābhavanaṃ praviśya bhuvi viśrutāṃ vilāsavatīm &

children.translated_text: meant for the wealthy, though he himself had meager resources. (4.16)

body.translated_text: There, entering a courtesan's house, he enjoyed <s>Vilāsavatī</s>, a famous courtesan of the land,

children.translated_text: she placed her entire treasure-store of various gems and gold under his control. (4.17)

body.translated_text: Seeing him as a worthy vessel bearing royal marks, of great substance,

children.translated_text: overcome with wonder, lovingly declared in private her great nobility: (4.18)

body.translated_text: Observing her natural and unstinting love and propriety, the king,

body.text: citramiyaṃ bahu vittaṃ kṣapayati veśyāpi matkṛte tṛṇavat &

children.translated_text: the love of courtesans, set free on the path of affection, is bound only to wealth.' (4.19)

body.translated_text: 'How remarkable—this courtesan too spends vast wealth for my sake as if it were straw;

children.text: tadapi dhanaṃ visṛjati yā kastasyāḥ premṇi saṃdehaḥ // 4.20 //
children.translated_text: but she who gives away wealth—who can doubt her love?' (4.20)

body.translated_text: 'Courtesans display false love out of greed for a morsel of wealth;

body.text: iti vacanaṃ bhūmipateḥ śrutvā vihasya sāsūyaḥ &

children.translated_text: and said to him, 'O king, who can trust the conduct of courtesans? (4.21)

body.translated_text: Hearing the king's words, the minister laughed with sarcasm

children.translated_text: sweet-tongued, enter the hearts of the undiscriminating. (4.22)

body.translated_text: 'These courtesans, devoid of truth, absorbed in tiny gains of wealth, dependent on moments of pleasure,

children.translated_text: bearing fruit of sorrow in the end—such are both hopes and courtesans for men. (4.23)

body.translated_text: 'Giving pleasure at the first meeting, causing ruin and exile in the middle,

body.text: adyāpi hariharādibhiḥ amarairapi tattvato na vijñātāḥ &

children.translated_text: courtesans and the illusions of <s>saṃsāra</s>, full of error, confusion, and delusion.' (4.24)

body.translated_text: 'Even to this day, even by <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and other immortals, they are not truly understood—

body.text: iti sacivavaco nṛpatiḥ śrutvā kṛtvā ca saṃvidaṃ tena &

children.translated_text: feigned his own death to test the courtesan. (4.25)

body.translated_text: Hearing the minister's words, the king, making an agreement with him,

children.translated_text: suddenly <s>Vilāsavatī</s>, fully adorned, proceeded toward the fire. (4.26)

body.translated_text: When, with the minister arranging the funeral pyre around that corpse-like body,

children.translated_text: the king, embracing her with both arms, joyfully declared, 'I am alive!' (4.27)

body.translated_text: As she rushed toward the fierce, blazing, brilliant flames of fire,

body.text: tattasyāḥ prema dṛḍhaṃ satyaṃ ca vicārya saṃbhṛtasnehaḥ &

children.translated_text: repeatedly reproached the minister, now favorable toward the virtues of courtesans. (4.28)

body.translated_text: Having examined that her love was firm and true, the king, deeply moved with affection,

children.translated_text: and raised a formidable army of elephants, horses, and soldiers. (4.29)

body.translated_text: Then the king took the courtesan's vast accumulated wealth, now under his control,

children.translated_text: regained his own kingdom, full and joy-giving like the moon. (4.30)

body.translated_text: With massive assembled forces, having conquered the rulers of the earth, that king

children.translated_text: shone like <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune), slender, her locks stirred by the breeze of <s>cāmara</s> fans. (4.31)

body.translated_text: And <s>Vilāsavatī</s>, placed by the king at the head of the harem ladies,

children.text: ūce nātha mayā tvaṃ kalpataruḥ sevitaściraṃ dāsyā // 4.32 //
children.translated_text: and said, 'O lord, I, your servant, have long served you as a wish-fulfilling tree. (4.32)

body.translated_text: Then once, in private, the courtesan approached the king with joined hands, bowing,

body.text: yadi nāma kutracidahaṃ yātā te hetutāṃ vibho lakṣmyāḥ &

children.translated_text: then please, by your grace, fulfill one wish of mine. (4.33)

body.translated_text: 'If indeed I have in some way been the cause of your prosperity, O lord,

children.text: tīrthānāmiva mahatāṃ na hi nāma samāgamo viphalaḥ // 4.34 //
children.translated_text: free from impurity, naturally pure—is never fruitless, (4.34)

body.translated_text: 'Just as the company of the great, like sacred fords—attainable through meritorious deeds,

body.text: abhavanmama ko'pi yuvā dayito dhanajīvitādhikaḥ praṇayī &

children.translated_text: he was imprisoned in the <s>Vidarbha</s> city, by fate's decree, as a thief.' (4.35)

body.translated_text: 'I once had a certain young man, dearer to me than wealth and life, a lover;

body.text: tanmuktaye mayā tvaṃ śaktataraḥ sevito mahīnāthaḥ &

children.translated_text: now do what is fitting for your valor, your lineage, and your heroism.' (4.36)

body.translated_text: 'For his liberation I served you, the most capable king;

body.text: iti vañcanāmavāpto vismita iva tadvaco nṛpaḥ śrutvā &

children.translated_text: gazing at the ground for a long time, recalled the minister's words. (4.37)

body.translated_text: Thus having received the deception, the king, hearing her words as if astonished,

body.text: atha tāṃ tathaiva rājāśvāsya vidarbheṣu bhūbhujaṃ jitvā &

children.translated_text: and arranged her reunion with her thief-lover, freed from prison. (4.38)

body.translated_text: Then, consoling her as before, the king conquered the ruler of <s>Vidarbha</s>

children.text: tattvena satyarahitāḥ ko jānāti sphuṭaṃ veśyāḥ // 4.39 //
children.translated_text: truly devoid of truth—who can fully know courtesans? (4.39)

body.translated_text: Thus, having many hearts, many tongues, many hands, and many deceptions,

children.translated_text: another the lover for protection, and another the lover for sport—such are the courtesans' men. (4.40)

body.translated_text: One is the lover by description, another by wealth, another by servant-labor,
Canto 5

body.text: moho nāma janānāṃ sarvaharo harati buddhimevādau &

children.text: gūḍhataraḥ sa ca nivasati kāyasthānāṃ mukhe ca lekhe ca // 5.1 //
children.translated_text: most secretly it dwells in the mouths and documents of <s>kāyasthas</s> (scribes/accountants). (5.1)

body.translated_text: <s>Moha</s> (Delusion) by name—it robs people of everything, stealing their intellect first of all;

children.translated_text: it is devoured in an instant, utterly consumed—like the full moon by <s>Rāhu</s>'s phase. (5.2)

body.translated_text: Like a fierce <s>kalā</s> (phase), when the harvest has fully ripened,

children.translated_text: but the phases of scribes are not known by anyone, despite great effort. (5.3)

body.translated_text: The phases of <s>saṃsāra</s> are known by yogins who have abandoned passion and delusion;

children.text: diviraireva samastā grastā janatā na kālena // 5.4 //
children.translated_text: the entire populace is devoured—not by Time itself, but by scribes. (5.4)

body.translated_text: By scribes with hundreds of camps of fraudulent arts, who create holes in people's wealth, whose ruin-bringing darkness destroys—

children.translated_text: demons of calculation and enumeration, they roam the world with birch-bark banners. (5.5)

body.translated_text: For these are the men of <s>Kāla</s> (Death), striking people with the fall of enormous punishments,

children.text: vrajati na yasya viṣaktaḥ kaṇṭhe pāśaḥ kṛtāntena // 5.6 //
children.translated_text: one around whose neck Death's noose is not fastened? (5.6)

body.translated_text: Who would trust those who are crooked as the tips of <s>Yama</s>'s buffalo's horns—

children.translated_text: with collyrium-like teardrops—the glory of the kingdom, being excavated by scribes, weeps as if in distress. (5.7)

body.translated_text: Ink flowing from the tip of a reed-pen, in the guise of drops,

body.translated_text: 'Having eaten a hundred-year-old <s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan) fruit, I have come from <s>Śrīparvata</s>' —

children.translated_text: who can know the hundreds of thousands of deceptions of cheaters? // 9.73 //

body.translated_text: These sixty-four tricks have been described by me in brief;

body.text:
iti mahākaviśrīkṣemendraviracite kalāvilāse nānādhūrtavarṇanaṃ nāma navamaḥ
sargaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth <s>sarga</s> (canto), named 'Description of Various Rogues,' in the <s>Kalāvilāsa</s> composed by the great poet <s>Śrī Kṣemendra</s>.
Canto 10

body.text: etā vañcakamāyā vijñeyā na tu punaḥ svayaṃ sevyāḥ &

children.translated_text: this collection of arts pertaining to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) is desired by the wise for prosperity. // 10.1 //

body.translated_text: These tricks of deceivers should be known, but not practiced by oneself;

children.translated_text: generosity, forgiveness, freedom from envy, truthfulness, absence of greed, and graciousness. // 10.2 //

body.translated_text: The foremost art of <s>dharma</s> is called compassion for beings, and benevolence toward others,

children.translated_text: knowing when to leave one's position, shrewdness, freedom from anxiety, and distrust toward women. // 10.3 //

body.translated_text: Of <s>artha</s> (wealth): constant industriousness, observance of regulations, knowledge of action,

children.translated_text: various kinds of <s>līlā</s> (amorous play), and understanding the minds of beloved ones. // 10.4 //

body.translated_text: Of <s>kāma</s> (pleasure): splendor of attire, elegance, charm, excellence of qualities,

children.translated_text: abandonment of worldly association, abiding in one's own dissolution, and the radiance of supreme love. // 10.5 //

body.translated_text: Of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation): delight in discrimination, tranquility, destruction of craving, and contentment,

children.translated_text: they are the true knowledge of those learned ones who conquer the deceivers of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). // 10.6 //

body.translated_text: These arts of the fourfold [aims of life], thirty-two in number, held in sequence, taken all together —

children.text: vairāgyaṃ ca parārthe sukhasya siddhāḥ kalāḥ pañca // 10.7 //
children.translated_text: and detachment for the sake of others — these are the five accomplished arts of happiness. // 10.7 //

body.translated_text: Abandonment of jealousy, pleasant speech, patience with steadfastness, freedom from anger,

children.translated_text: pure learning, and delight in fame — these seven are the root arts of good character. // 10.8 //

body.translated_text: Association with the virtuous, conquest of desire, purity, reverence for the teacher, right conduct,

children.translated_text: boldness, good companions, gratitude, guarding of counsel, and generosity,

body.translated_text: Splendor, courage, intelligence, enterprise, statesmanship, knowledge of gestures and intentions,

children.translated_text: and tender care for dependents — these are the seventeen arts of authority. // 10.10 //

body.translated_text: affection, discernment, winning of friends, compassion, absence of pride,

children.translated_text: these sixty-four arts should be acquired by the wise. // 10.11 //

body.translated_text: Silence, freedom from fickleness, and not begging — these three arts are the life of honor;

children.translated_text: righteous conduct for the afflicted; fortitude in sorrow; absence of pride in happiness. // 10.12 //

body.translated_text: When opposed by the powerful, one should go to them, or bow to them; when strength rises, enmity;

children.translated_text: turning away from the contemptible — this is the tenfold remedy of arts. // 10.13 //

body.translated_text: Sharing of wealth in prosperity; delight in the virtuous; wisdom in doubtful counsel;

children.translated_text: greed is the worst of sins; anger is the cause of all afflictions. // 10.14 //

body.translated_text: The words of the guru are foremost among truths; worship of cows, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and gods is foremost among duties;

children.translated_text: servitude is the worst of sorrows; hope is a serpent's noose over vast time. // 10.15 //

body.translated_text: Wisdom is the fame-giver among all virtues; abundant wealth is the source of magnificence;

children.translated_text: begging destroys honor; poverty is a caravan of afflictions. // 10.16 //

body.translated_text: Generosity is the jewel-mine of treasures; freedom from enmity is the abode of happiness;

children.translated_text: vice is a host of diseases; laziness is the destroyer of household prosperity. // 10.17 //

body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is the provision for the journey; truth is the purifier of the lotus-face;

children.translated_text: arrogance produces darkness; hypocrisy is an object of universal ridicule. // 10.18 //

body.translated_text: Desirelessness is the most praiseworthy; kind speech is the sweetest of all;

children.translated_text: slander brings displeasure; cutting off livelihood is the conduct of the cruel. // 10.19 //

body.translated_text: Non-malice is purity; steadiness is the special observance of vows;

children.translated_text: deceit belongs to the deluded; ingratitude is the cause of falling into hell. // 10.20 //

body.translated_text: Compassion is the merit of virtues; gratitude is the mark of a true person;

children.translated_text: the cruel one is an outcaste; the deceitful one is an incarnation of the <s>Kali Yuga</s>. // 10.21 //

body.translated_text: <s>Madana</s> (passion) belongs to fickle thieves; women's words cause division among kinsmen;

children.translated_text: old age brings afflictions; illness brings suffering equal to death. // 10.22 //

body.translated_text: <s>Śāstra</s> (scripture) is a jewel-lamp; instruction is an anointing;

children.translated_text: a wife is the essence of the household; a son is a kinsman in the next world. // 10.23 //

body.translated_text: Attachment is a treacherous poison; passion for a courtesan is like spreading leprosy;

children.translated_text: youth is the delight of women; beauty is a feast of charming adornment and attire. // 10.24 //

body.translated_text: An enemy is a hundred thorns; a wicked son is the ruin of the family;

children.translated_text: worry causes withering; hatred is a fire burning in a hollow tree. // 10.25 //

body.translated_text: Contentment is sovereignty; association with the virtuous is the glory of a universal emperor;

children.translated_text: timidity brings illness; crookedness is a waterless dark well. // 10.26 //

body.translated_text: Friendship is the source of trust; freedom from restraint is the enjoyment of great pleasures;

children.translated_text: gambling is the worst of vices; being conquered by a woman makes one a ghost on a desert bank. // 10.27 //

body.translated_text: Uprightness produces purity; humility is a crown of the finest jewels;

children.translated_text: friendship with the wicked is fickle; service of evil men is a waste of effort. // 10.28 //

body.translated_text: Renunciation is a bracelet of gems; learning is a brilliant jewel for the ear;

children.translated_text: delight in truth is the rarest attainment; an assembly of fools destroys sound discrimination. // 10.29 //

body.translated_text: Bliss is a garden; seeing a loved one is a shower of nectar;

children.translated_text: the royal court is a place of suspicion; a woman's heart is crooked by nature. // 10.30 //

body.translated_text: A man of good family is a fruit-bearing tree; good fortune is an incarnation of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>;

children.translated_text: a daughter brings sorrow; one devoid of intelligence deserves compassion. // 10.31 //

body.translated_text: Propriety is the most praiseworthy; appreciation of merit is like an anointing of sandalwood;

children.translated_text: liquor belongs to ghouls; hunting belongs to elephants, jungles, and <s>yakṣas</s>. // 10.32 //

body.translated_text: Wealth is the source of good fortune; the affection of people is the root of fame;

children.translated_text: the greedy man is fruitless; one devoid of right conduct is a cremation ground. // 10.33 //

body.translated_text: Tranquility produces well-being; delight in the self is the pilgrimage of pilgrimages;

children.translated_text: envy produces a hundred consumptions; infamy is a death by leprosy. // 10.34 //

body.translated_text: Statecraft is the protection of women; conquest of the senses is the source of power;

children.translated_text: murder is the sharpest of sharp deeds; cutting is the weapon of the sharpest blades. // 10.35 //

body.translated_text: A mother is the most auspicious; a father is the teacher of meritorious celebrations;

children.translated_text: honor is nourishing; fame is the essence of worldly existence. // 10.36 //

body.translated_text: A bow removes anger; cordiality is the resort of difficult requests;

children.translated_text: humility brings auspiciousness; enthusiasm is the key to all accomplishments. // 10.37 //

body.translated_text: Devotion to the lord is the course of the righteous; death in battle is the path to bliss;

children.translated_text: fame in this <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is the most essential thing for all people. // 10.38 //

body.translated_text: Merit is the most attainable; knowledge is the supreme illumination;

children.translated_text: as the most excellent in this world, like a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> among all <s>varṇas</s> (classes). // 10.39 //

body.translated_text: He who is skilled in the collection of arts, the knower of the truth of all things, should be recognized

children.translated_text: for him alone, in worldly affairs, <s>Lakṣmī</s> (the goddess of fortune) is seen with visible purpose. // 10.40 //

body.translated_text: Thus has been spoken this century of verses; he who knows the arts of auspicious and inauspicious outcomes —

children.translated_text: spent the night in his own mansion, where moonbeams blossomed like flower buds. // 10.41 //

body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Mūladeva</s>, dismissing his disciples and performing the customary rites,

children.text: lokopadeśaviṣayaḥ sukathāvicitro bhūyātsatāṃ dayita eṣa kalāvilāsaḥ // 10.42 //
children.translated_text: a subject of instruction for the world, rich in beautiful tales — may this <s>Kalāvilāsa</s> be dear to the virtuous! // 10.42 //

body.translated_text: Full of playfulness, delightful with the arts of smiles and grace, a lamp illuminating the arts within the heart of every being,

children.translated_text: like the moon, may it always bring joy to the minds of the virtuous. // 10.43 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Kalāvilāsa</s>, risen from the ocean of <s>Kṣemendra's</s> genius,

body.text:
iti mahākaviśrīkṣemendraviracite kalāvilāse sakalakalānirūpaṇaṃ nāma daśamaḥ
sargaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth <s>sarga</s> (canto), named 'Delineation of All Arts,' in the <s>Kalāvilāsa</s> composed by the great poet <s>Śrī Kṣemendra</s>.
